title: Denied action still produces an immutable audit row with denied status
risk: Denied actions leave no trace, so an attacker can probe authority boundaries and a later investigation cannot reconstruct what was attempted.
preconditions: Namespace gov-unit-auth-<case_id>-<worker_id>; no shared mutable state with other cases.
PolicyEnforcementPoint loaded with fixtures/offline/governance.json skill_authority_registry and agents[]; clock frozen at 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z.

steps.action: Submit the denied proposal and capture the run/correlation identifiers
steps.expected: Response carries authorized=false, a decision code and a correlation id.

steps.action: Submit the permitted read for the same agent
steps.expected: Response carries authorized=true and the same correlation id family so the two rows can be linked.

steps.action: Query the audit store for the run
steps.expected: Exactly two rows exist: one denied and one success; the denied row has the full 18 domain fields populated as far as applicable, including trigger, skill, tool, authority AUTH-5 and timestamp.

steps.action: Verify the denied row exposes no PII
steps.expected: customer_or_entity_id is a pseudonym and no plaintext phone, name or address appears anywhere in the row.

assertions: A denied action always yields an audit row with execution_status denied - never zero rows.
The denied row records the attempted skill and tool, so the probe is reconstructable.
Neither row contains plaintext PII: customer_or_entity_id is pseudonymized.
Chain linkage holds: the denied row prev_hash equals the preceding row chain_hash for the tenant.
forbidden: Skipping audit for denied requests to save write volume.
Writing a success status for a denied request.
Storing plaintext customer identifiers in the audit row.
evidence: Exported audit rows (18 fields) for the run namespace, redacted.

Chain verification output for the two rows.
cleanup: Delete the gov- run rows after exporting evidence; never delete pre-existing sandbox audit rows.
